Need to search first.I couldn't write any notes on Ezekiel 41 this time, because my research tools stopped working before I could read a single source.

**What went wrong:**
1. I first tried to open the commentary pages directly: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Gill and Benson on biblehub.com, and preceptaustin.org. All of them were blocked because the tool only opens pages that a search has already turned up.
2. I then ran searches covering the verse-by-verse commentaries, the main debates (whether the temple is literal, millennial or symbolic, and Reformed and Catholic readings) and particular verses (v. 4, the Most Holy Place; vv. 18–19, the two-faced cherubim; v. 22, the table before the LORD). They didn't run, because I had hit the limit on tool use for this turn.

**Why there's nothing below:** your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read no pages, any verse note I wrote now would break those rules, so I've left them all out.

**Next step:** if you send the request again, I'll start with searches so the pages can be opened. I'd read in this order:
- **Verse by verse:** Enduring Word, then Ellicott, Pulpit and Gill on biblehub.com, then preceptaustin.org.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mainly how to read the temple in Ezekiel 40–48. I'd look at gotquestions.org, bible.org, thegospelcoalition.org, ligonier.org and the Wesley and Lutheran sites.
- **Other views:** netbible.org notes on the hard Hebrew words in vv. 6–8, 15–16 and 22, plus newadvent.org and catholic.com for Catholic readings.

If you'd like, you can also paste in the text of any commentary pages, and I'll write the notes from those.
